message: 58M. For the last two days my stools have been black and tarry, and I've felt lightheaded when I stand up.

basis.quote: For the last two days my stools have been black and tarry
basis.interpretation: Black tarry stools (melena) indicate upper gastrointestinal bleeding; two-day duration represents active or recent bleeding

basis.quote: I've felt lightheaded when stand up
basis.interpretation: Orthostatic lightheadedness suggests possible volume depletion or hemodynamic compromise secondary to blood loss

output.reason: Active gastrointestinal bleeding (melena) with orthostatic symptoms requires immediate emergency evaluation, resuscitation capability, and possible transfusion or endoscopic intervention.

question.text: Have you vomited any blood, or noticed any other symptoms like abdominal pain, nausea, or dizziness while lying down?
question.why: Hematemesis and associated symptoms would refine bleeding severity and location; ongoing symptoms at rest versus only with position change clarify hemodynamic significance.

output.reason: 58-year-old with two days of black tarry stools (melena) plus lightheadedness on standing suggests ongoing GI bleeding with possible significant blood volume loss; this requires immediate emergency assessment, IV access, bloodwork and possible endoscopy that messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Call 911 now and go to an emergency department; do not drive yourself. Black tarry stools usually mean bleeding in the upper digestive tract, and feeling lightheaded when you stand can mean you have lost enough blood to affect your circulation — this needs urgent in-person testing and treatment. While waiting, stay lying down, avoid eating or drinking, and if you faint, vomit blood or become confused, tell the dispatcher immediately.
differential: Upper GI bleed (e.g. peptic ulcer, gastritis, varices) presenting as melena
Small bowel or right-colonic bleeding source
Acute blood-loss anemia with orthostatic intolerance
